rows.title: A trivial Bash call waited on the full work of the heavy Bash hooks
rows.note: The llm-legs half of the same pour is llm-legs@c85ff90 (instruction-write-gate read-only note, worker-launch-gate early exit, instruction-files batched realpath). 2026-10-01 (second fix): the 48bfc77 fast path covered the heavy hooks, but the setters had moved to hooks that still forked per payload field. commit-report parses its payload once (jq 4 -> 1 on ls, 138 -> 75 ms isolated); english-gate exits on the shared readonly-command classifier before sourcing review-journal for launch parsing (git status 101 -> 56 ms, a non-read-only call unchanged at 91 ms; a read-only command never names a launcher, so no launch is missed); worker-git-guard, the before-side setter at 394 ms (34%), parses once instead of a jq -e validation plus a jq per field (main-session ls 167 -> 72 ms). Process-count asserts in test_commit_report, test_english_gates and test_worker_git_guard are red on the old hooks. At 08:37 the floor read 790 ms under 100% CPU (10 suites at once). Left: worker-tag-hook forks 2 jq before its exit on a plain Bash call; worker-edit-guard none.

rows.title: context-nudge read a 1 MiB transcript tail through jq on every tool call
rows.note: Design §4: 79 ms a call before the 64 KiB tail read, 62 ms after; its own tail read cut it, not the fast path.

rows.title: An Edit or Write waits over 500 ms on hooks: edit-conflict-notice before, commit-journal after
rows.note: Design §7.1 calibration: 655 ms on 2026-09-29; 549 ms in the live run of 2026-09-29 21:18. 2026-09-30: 768 ms p50 = edit-conflict-notice 390 ms before + commit-journal 280 / instruction-watch check 237 ms after. The before side was live_run_holder forking head, sed and a same_owner subshell per unswept worker-run record of every repository (46 records); it now reads them with builtins and asks same_owner only of a record that concerns the file. The after side is the hooks run of the same night (hook_every_call / hook_grows_* on commit-journal and instruction-watch check); see the handoff.

rows.title: A non-trivial Bash call waits over 500 ms on hooks
rows.note: Setters: review-flow-gate before, commit-journal after (both claude-setup); their shared cost is the content snapshot pair (rj_snapshot_repos ~130 of 412 traced ms). 2026-10-03 09:45, 24 h: before p50 462 ms (338 without review-flow-gate), after 376 ms (269 without commit-journal); paired p50 over 500 ms in all 22 hours (558-1849), 467-1010 with both setters removed, CPU busy 0.9-1.0 in 20 of them and 791 ms at busy 0.57: the ~17-hook bash fan-out per side is structural, not only night load. Next setters once both drop: worker-launch-gate before (302 ms), instruction-watch check after (271 ms). Every one of them is a problem of the same night's hooks run (09-30, 10-01 and 10-03 alike), which holds the claude-setup worktree; no hook-waits run had one, so none changed a hook. Ruled out: the 4ca8de1 session-repo fan-out (381 vs 459 ms at 5+ repos, most calls in 1-2), instruction-watch check as a setter while commit-journal is slower (moves the after side 9-11 ms), vendor replacement of attribution snapshots (none found), a fixer limit change. See the handoff.

rows.title: suites · llm-legs doubles its wall clock when several full runs share the machine
rows.note: Narrowed to concurrent full runs: the 1326 s run of 2026-09-30 02:29 local overlapped three other full llm-legs runs (02:24 2060 s, 02:38 1538 s, 02:39 1463 s; logdirs under $TMPDIR/run-suites.*), each -j 5 on 10 cores. Its summed suite time was 6506 s against about 2200 s in quiet runs, and wall ≈ summed/5, so the run was throughput-bound; no suite regressed. The design accepts it: run-suites has no cross-invocation lock, and handoff 2026-09-28 §4 forbids a cross-chat queue. Cause still stands on 2026-10-01; concurrent full runs sharing the machine continue to double wall clock. 2026-10-02: the stated cause no longer stands in code: llm-legs@badbf8f caps the machine at RUN_SUITES_SLOTS full runs (cores/3, 2 to 4; share/run-suites.sh:128) and the wall clock starts after the slot wait, so four overlapping runs cannot recur. Left open, not fixed: three runs at -j cores/2 still oversubscribe the cores, and tonight's load average of ~125-130 came from outside run-suites, which no suite-side change can absorb; the next quiet-machine run decides it.

rows.title: test_worker_run · llm-legs 24 h cost exceeds 2 h limit due to frequent runs and concurrent load
rows.note: test_worker_run.sh is 7727 lines with ~300 test cases exercising the worker-run CLI lifecycle. Quiet runs take 600-654 s wall clock, and under concurrent load (multiple full test suites running at -j 5) runs take 962-1186 s. Over 24 h, 26 runs accumulated 12535 s (>3.5 h), exceeding the 7200 s limit. Splitting the suite across multiple test files or raising limits requires architectural coordination with the owner chats (Harness Doctor and llm-workers). 2026-10-01: split into sixteen tests/test_worker_run_<part>.sh suites over tests/worker_run_harness.sh, which run-suites runs in parallel; the ident follows every part, so a part that grows back into a long pole or a daily cost still lands on this row.

rows.title: Unaccounted CPU is the fork and exec cost of parallel test suites and statusline renders
rows.note: Fork and exec of requested parallel work. 2026-10-03 07:30-09:30 local: 8.4 of 10 cores unseen, kernel 60 %, ~745 000 page faults/s (~180 000 copy-on-write); 30 s ancestor census 1 350-1 840 new proc/s: test suites 44-62 %, statusline 19-25 %, hooks 8-19 %, worker-run 9 %. Ruled out: memory compression (~200 decompressions/s); a run-suites over-subscription (three RUN_SUITES_SLOTS held, as capped); night worker count (NIGHT_FIXER_SLOTS, badbf8f); worker-run's supervisor 10 ms poll (start-up only). The statusline is llm-legs bin/statusline.sh, not claude-setup: ~65-100 bash subshells a render, review-debt Python every 15 s per shown tree (0.73 CPU-s); staleness-free fork cuts save ~1 % of forks, larger ones are item 2 of docs/handoffs/2026-09-28-harness-performance-fix.md (Egor's word). Same ground re-measured by load fixers 2026-09-30 to 2026-10-03; the remaining decision is the judge's, in the handoff.

rows.title: The tripwire journaled writes another record already carried, so one write counted as growth twice
rows.note: Event 5751c770d8700227 (2026-09-29T20:50:18Z, compaction SessionStart of a session whose own baseline dated from before 2026-09-28T19:43Z) listed 20 files: 15 synced-skill files and hammerspoon/CLAUDE.md whose alert marks earlier checks had claimed (20:14-20:33Z, 09:39Z), and review-tiers.md whose 2026-09-28T19:43Z record had outlived its one-day mark. alert_once now journals only the files this check claimed, and a mark lives past the baselines' week-old sweep. Follow-up 2026-10-01: The regression now includes 6bbd8cc122eaaeea (2026-09-30T09:42:45Z, 15 google-workspace files) and e4a27d26b246bec2 (2026-10-01T01:12:13Z, six math-proof files plus a 33-byte README). Math-proof was already reported by watcher 6abd5e9b7ca01b57 at 19:10:19Z. Current alert_once filters claimed files; Lua watchEmit does too; both derive hash@mtime via the same watch_mark_key and accept w-suffixed markers. Thus the original whole-batch re-journaling implementation is already removed. Historical records carry no hash@mtime, so an actual vendor rewrite versus expired/missing claim versus old resident watcher cannot be distinguished. Do not claim a dedup fix or suppress between-sessions. Owner must obtain write-key/runtime-version evidence and reproduce watcher-first then resumed-baseline behavior. Existing tripwire-duplicate-records blind spot remains applicable.

rows.title: Background work that never ends held every end-of-turn ask for hours: a Storybook server, a night-job Monitor, agents launched one after another (35 h in one chat)
rows.note: stop-dispatch.sh holds asks for background work at most STOP_DISPATCH_HELD_CAP (3600 s), then runs them at that stop with busy empty and the journal line's held naming what it would have called busy, and the hold restarts; ask-span-drill stays silent under STOP_HELD; ask-run-unfinished also sees waiter tasks under the 2.1.285 label subagent. The doctor's ask-busy rule does not see asks run under held, by design. The 2026-09-30 06:55-08:16 regression was transitional (tasks started before e5909cd landed). The 2026-10-01 regression (10896605, 10:17-13:08Z, 10269 s) was the 959efae stale-hold rule misfiring: no stop from 10:32 to 12:11Z because a task notification at 11:40Z opened a 31-min turn, the old tasks ended inside it and a new one started, so 'no stop for the cap and none of its tasks live' restarted the hold of a live chat. The held file is now 'since chat-pid' ($PPID, the Claude Code process: hook-time rows show one stable ppid per chat process) and only a different process (a closed chat resumed) restarts it; old-format files restart once. Ruled out: notice timing, ask-span-drill, worker-run holds (busy was bg-task throughout). Risk to watch: a harness that wrapped hooks in a per-call shell would restart every hold and bring the unbounded hold back; this rule would show it.

rows.title: notice-word-journal.sh timed out (exit 124) at the stops of a chat with a 47 MB transcript

rows.title: commit-journal over 50 ms on every write call
rows.note: Narrowed: the multi-repository part is cut by hook-grows-repos-commit-journal; what stays is its floor on a one-repository call (bash, the 2.4k-line review-journal.sh source at ~20-40 ms, jq, one git status). 2026-10-03: the 811-853 ms p50 was the night orchestrator (191 of 355 heavy runs, p50 1050 ms wall / 972 ms CPU): a worker records under its launcher, so the launcher's .repos named 11 worker worktrees, each snapshotted before and after every launcher call; claude-setup@9171da1 lets a read-only Bash call out before the library, and claude-setup@7837e81 snapshots over .repos minus .repos.workers (trees first listed by a worker and not written in by the launcher since; a tree already listed before stays snapshotted). Other chats: p50 363 ms, dominated by the repositories they register (logo-vectorizer-bench: 33 704 untracked paths, 0.5-1.5 s a snapshot). Under 50 ms needs a design change or a different limit: the owner's.

rows.title: commit-journal over 150 ms a run
rows.note: 853 ms p50 at first sight (2026-10-03), the same runs as hook-every-call-commit-journal: the orchestrator's launcher-registry sweep (cut in claude-setup@9171da1) plus the snapshot floor of the repositories a chat registers. What stays after the cut is that floor (p50 363 ms outside the orchestrator at load 60-90), driven by large untracked trees such as logo-vectorizer-bench. Under 150 ms needs a cheaper snapshot (an untracked-cache or fsmonitor git status, or skipping trees over a size) or a different limit: the owner's.

rows.title: instruction-watch check over 50 ms on every write call
rows.note: Narrowed: the ~/.claude walk no longer descends file-history and its path spelling runs tr instead of perl (llm-legs share/instruction-files.sh); the watch set is cut 468 to 183 rows (hook-p50-instruction-watch-baseline). What stays is the floor of about 20 process starts; 2026-10-03 profile (224 ms at load 90): library source ~21 ms, instruction_repo_files' three git ls-files ~31 ms, the $(instruction_watch_state) subshells ~28 ms. Under 50 ms needs a cached enumeration (keyed on the repos' index mtimes) or a different limit: the owner's.

rows.title: report-flush slower in chats with 5+ repositories
rows.note: Not contention (the 2026-09-30 theory): report-bus flush ran prune on every call, one stat per delivered report, so the cost grew with a chat's age and its worker count, largest in orchestrators (the 5+-repository chats). Prune now runs only over its 200-report cap and a flush with nothing pending and no cap returns before any read: 789-1211 ms to 40-72 ms in a chat with 86 delivered reports at load 90; test_report_bus asserts no stat on a 199-report flush.

rows.title: instruction-watch check slower in transcripts over 10 MB
rows.note: Narrowed to a confound: the quiet check reads no transcript (only revert_growth does, on a changed guarded file); its cost is the constant watch-set enumeration plus load_inflight's scan of machine-wide marks, the same for every chat. Sessions over 10 MB are the orchestrators, whose calls run under more sibling hooks and load. 2026-10-03: code path re-read, still no transcript read on the quiet path. Dismissal proposed in the handoff.

rows.title: A chat start waits over 1000 ms on hooks
rows.note: 2026-10-01: 1797.691 ms fresh floor, launch 1772.148 ms; 3300 ms at 08:37 with the CPU 100% busy under the night's suites. instruction-watch baseline remains the named setter; cmd_baseline compares with the newest baseline, and cmd_check exits after writing it, so the following write_baseline is not a duplicate on that path. Batched stat, shasum and snapshot-key hashing already exist; ranked refresh is mtime/version gated. No evidence that compact-auto or session-trash set this floor. Same-night harness-hooks-20261001T020656Z-42ed owns hook_p50:instruction-watch.sh baseline; changing its trust/snapshot path concurrently is handed off. That run committed llm-legs@d31376b on its branch (the baseline walk prunes ~/.claude trees nothing loads, 3.1 s -> 1.46 s); judge this floor after its merge.

rows.title: A turn end waits over 1000 ms on hooks
rows.note: 2026-10-01: 1335.809 ms over 28 stops; 3510 ms at 08:37 under full CPU load. stop-dispatch runs notices in parallel already, then asks in order; blanket parallelization would change notice-before-ask and first-block behavior. It still launches jq per journal record (record() and final hooks_json); batching that encoding is a candidate for harness-hooks-20261001T020656Z-42ed, which owns hook_p50:stop-dispatch.sh. Stop guards also belong to harness-stop-hooks-20261001T020700Z-5bfd. No vendor replacement found for the custom busy/held and journal contract. The hooks run committed claude-setup@c9f579c on its branch (the chat-name notice parsed the whole transcript, 1.3 s of a 2.9 s stop); judge this floor after its merge.

rows.title: Another tool call waits over 300 ms on hooks
rows.note: 2026-10-01: fresh floor 396.22 ms over 77 calls; worker-spawn-hook sets the before side and context-nudge the after side. worker-spawn-hook now parses its payload once (one @sh-quoted jq array instead of a jq per field); prompt newlines, ATTACH routing, model stripping and session sanitation kept. Isolated probe under load: fork spawn 254 -> 154 ms (jq 11 -> 2), codex-worker 286 -> 226 ms (jq 9 -> 2), Workflow early return jq 3 -> 1. At 08:37 (CPU 100% busy) the floor read 3485 ms over 12 calls with worker-limit-gate before (hook_p50:worker-limit-gate.sh, 3.5 s, new after this run's launch, left for the next run) and report-flush after. GROKB_MODELS_NO_FETCH already prevents a model refresh, so no network-refresh change is needed. context-nudge still needs the current token window after tools: a blanket read-only skip would miss the assistant token growth. Its 64 KiB tail/sidecar path remains. Live floor recovery is unconfirmed until post-merge exposure; no quiet rows were supplied in this packet.

rows.title: instruction-watch baseline watched ~/.claude trees nothing loads, and every baseline carried them forward
rows.note: 285 of 468 watched rows sat under ~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces (catalog clones the harness auto-update pulls; installed plugins load from plugins/cache), plugins/.trash and a hidden top-level backup. Pruning the walk alone changed nothing: the between-sessions check pins every row of the newest baseline, so the set only grew. Now the walk prunes them and every baseline row and visible path under them is dropped (INSTRUCTION_HOME_UNLOADED_ERE). A/B on a copy of the live state, alternating runs: baseline 3.1 s to 1.46 s at load ~140, 5.0 s to 2.6 s at load ~330; quiet check 1.13 s to 0.94 s at load ~330. Also ends the false CHANGED reports on marketplace README pulls (21 log lines). Ruled out: the walk itself (17-25 ms), the reverts/ directory (maxdepth 1 never descends it). Test: tests/test_instruction_watch_perf.py three unloaded-tree cases.

rows.title: the chat-name Stop notice parsed the whole transcript at every turn end
rows.note: notice-chat-names (lib/chat_names.py last_assistant_text) json-parsed every line of the transcript to find the last assistant row: 1.3 s of a 2.9 s stop on a 39 MB transcript, the longest of the parallel notices, so the dispatcher's critical path. It now reads from the end with a growing window: 938 ms to 240 ms on that transcript (Python start dominates the rest). Ruled out: the backstop (57-94 ms here; one live exit 124 at load 250 with 16 background tasks), the asks (under 200 ms), words_journal (full reads only on a turn a notice fired). Tests: test_stop_dispatch.sh, the tail-parse count (3002 parses on the old code) and an assistant row past the first window.

rows.title: instruction-watch check over 150 ms a run
rows.note: Narrowed: the watch set is cut 468 to 183 rows (hook-p50-instruction-watch-baseline), about 17 % of the quiet check under load. What stays is a process floor of about 20 starts (jq, git rev-parse, three git ls-files, perl, find, tr, realpath, stat, three awk, mkdir, touch) whatever the set; at load 100-300 each start costs 10 ms and more. Under 150 ms needs the cached enumeration of the 2026-09-30 handoff: the owner's.

rows.title: worker-launch-gate over 150 ms a run
rows.note: Narrowed to its process count: about 60 starts on a plain non-read-only Bash call (30 grep, 7 tr, 6 sed, 5 head, 5 awk, 4 jq, 2 realpath), most of them the owned-class checks run unconditionally; command length adds 10-20 % (13 KB heredoc vs 39 bytes). Not cut in a night run: it is a deny gate, and the cut (one jq, one grep -Eq over every owned regex before the per-class greps, wait_default read only for relay polls) needs its adversarial pass. Proposed in the handoff.

rows.title: worker-launch-gate slower in chats with 5+ repositories
rows.note: Narrowed to a confound: the gate reads only the command text; no repository, no registry, and a transcript only for a relay agent's worker-run start or a legs/scheduler hit. The chats with 5+ repositories are the orchestrators, whose calls run beside more sibling hooks and carry longer commands (+10-20 %). 2026-10-03: still stands, gate code unchanged; the real 5+-repository causes found in its siblings (stop-dispatch, worker-limit-gate 2026-10-02; report-flush's prune, commit-journal's launcher registry 2026-10-03) are not on its path. Dismissal proposed in the handoff.

rows.title: english-gate slower in chats with 5+ repositories
rows.note: Narrowed to a command-mix confound (259 ms against 96 at first sight, 2026-10-03): the gate reads no repository; its expensive path is a model launch (launch_args python plus cyrillic-share on the brief, ~400-600 ms), and 82 % of the night orchestrator's Bash calls are launches (review-bench fix/review/report, worker-run claim/report) against 1 % in other chats; common-path wall 132 ms there against 118 ms elsewhere. claude-setup@9171da1 cut the common path anyway (a launcher-token screen before the 2.4k-line library, 82-88 to 53-61 ms; er_over asks no --max for a zero share). Dismissal proposed in the handoff.

rows.title: worker-launch-gate slower in transcripts over 10 MB
rows.note: Narrowed to a confound, as hook-grows-repos-worker-launch-gate: no transcript read on the path every call takes. Dismissal proposed in the handoff.

rows.title: review-flow-gate over 150 ms a run
rows.note: Narrowed: the per-repository snapshot is parallel (claude-setup@4ca8de1); 2026-10-03 the 573-760 ms p50 was the orchestrator snapshotting its workers' worktrees from its own .repos; claude-setup@9171da1 and @7837e81 drop the workers' trees from that set (.repos.workers) and let a read-only call out before the library (write call with 5 registered trees 460-516 to 283-287 ms, read-only 67-70 to 43-44 ms, load 90). What stays is the snapshot floor of the trees a chat writes in (the same one hook-sync-commit-journal names). Design or limit: the owner's.

rows.title: test_review_bench · review-bench long pole exceeds 50% share of full test run
rows.note: test_review_bench.sh took 336 s of a 342 s run: one ~17,900-line Python heredoc, serial. 2026-10-02: split at section boundaries into tests/test_review_bench{,_panels,_lifecycle,_rounds}.sh over tests/review_bench_harness.{sh,py} (the shared preamble and hoisted fixtures, exec'd into each part's globals; each later part restores part 1's environment, lens registry and account patches), which run-suites runs in parallel; ~100-120 s per part under load average ~125. Every monolith line survives in some part (line-multiset check); the gateway-cooldown block sets REVIEW_BENCH_TRANSIENT_BACKOFF_S=0, dropping 31 s of real backoff sleeps it never asserted on. The ident follows every part, so a part that grows back into a long pole lands on this row.

rows.title: test_review_bench · review-bench suites journaled as llm-legs runs
rows.note: llm-legs has no test_review_bench suite: a worker launched in an llm-legs worktree ran review-bench's run-all (ADD-DIR), and statusline-work-probe.sh stamped the run with the worker's workdir repository. 2026-10-02: run rows carry the repository run-suites recorded in its progress file (field 10), the probe resolves that over the workdir, and test_test_journal asserts it; the pole itself shrank with the review-bench split. Rows journaled before the fix keep the wrong repository until they age out of the window.

rows.title: logo-vectorizer-bench over 13 400 loose git objects
rows.note: Writers: unreachable hash-object -w blobs of untracked bench outputs from llm-legs worker-run snapshots (14 620 of the 15 975 loose objects written 07-10 local on 10-03 are shas in dirty-before/after-shas of the 213 runs with workdir logo-vectorizer-bench since 10-01 22:00; the 10-02 fixer's 'no worker run since 09-30' was wrong) and claude-setup review-journal rj_hash_paths (the 10-02 burst). git gc --auto does not fix it: it only repacks reachable objects and leaves unreachable ones younger than gc.pruneExpire loose with a 'too many unreachable loose objects' warning, which under autoDetach becomes a gc.log that blocks auto gc for a day (git 2.49, reproduced in a scratch repo). Fix: worker-run pack_loose_objects runs the maintenance loose-objects task (threshold gc.auto, default 6 700) plus prune-packed after every after-snapshot, which packs any loose object of the repository, review-journal blobs included; tested in test_worker_run_files snapshot_blobs_packed_tests. Left: review-journal still never packs in a repository with chats and no worker runs (handoff); in a repository with no commits the loose-* packs are only consolidated by a manual gc (gc.autoPackLimit needs a commit or fetch to fire). Ruled out: gc.log, gc.auto=0, stashes, worktrees, night-run base snapshots.

rows.title: stop-dispatch ran its hooks one after another and forked per worker-run record
rows.note: The dispatcher's critical path was serial: the backstop, then the notices, then every ask one after another, and three of them (dispatcher, backstop, ask-run-unfinished) forked tr per unfinished worker-run record (22 of 732 tonight) to read its launcher; plus a jq per journal record and four for the payload. Now the launcher is read with a builtin, the backstop runs beside the notices, the asks run at once after them, and one jq builds the journal line. A/B at load 50-60 on the real run root: 1.24 s to 0.34 s on a small transcript. Ruled out as the dispatcher's own: Python start of the notices (~70-140 ms each, parallel).

rows.title: stop-dispatch slower in chats with 5+ repositories
rows.note: No repository read: the dispatcher reads no .repos registry. The 5+-repository chats are the orchestrators, with the largest transcripts and the most worker runs; both costs are cut by hook-sync-stop-dispatch and hook-grows-size-stop-dispatch.

rows.title: stop-dispatch slower in transcripts over 10 MB
rows.note: words_journal.readings parsed the whole transcript on the first stop of a turn the word intake printed a notice on (38 of 432 stops in 24 h): 0.9 s on 31 MB, 3.7 s on 129 MB, under notices running at once so the dispatcher's critical path. It now reads from the end, the window growing until it holds his last message (what precedes it never counts): 129 MB 3.7 s to 12 ms, identical lines on 24 real transcripts. With the hook-sync-stop-dispatch cuts, 31 MB with a notice ~2.0 s to ~0.9 s. Not cut: a transcript whose last human message is far back still walks to it (an autonomous span); the notice fires on his message, so the real case is near the end.

rows.title: worker-limit-gate waits on worker-pick's codex catalog walk
rows.note: worker-pick --account <vendor> ran `codexb models --own` once per codex account (7 here, ~130 ms each at load 50) for the codex catalog check added 2026-10-01 (e961a07), whatever vendor was asked; only the codex answer reads it. Now skipped for --account claudeb|gemini|grok: 1.4 s to 0.7 s. worker-limit-gate asks worker-pick on every vendor-worker spawn, and also expanded every absolute path of every spawn's prompt (realpath, wc, tr, cat each) though only a vendor worker's triage claim reads it; now done there alone. Gate with a stub picker: ~320 ms of its own at load 50, about 25 process starts, no single hot spot. What stays is worker-pick's own ~0.7 s floor (the whole table for one answer): the owner's, see the handoff.

rows.title: worker-limit-gate slower in chats with 5+ repositories
rows.note: No repository read. The 5+-repository chats are the orchestrators: they spawn vendor workers (each pays worker-pick, cut in hook-sync-worker-limit-gate) with long briefs naming many paths (the expansion, now done for a vendor worker's triage claim alone).

rows.title: worker-spawn-hook waits on worker-pick's codex catalog walk
rows.note: With a stub picker the hook takes ~55 ms at load 50 for every agent type; its cost is route_account, worker-pick --account for a brief with no ACCOUNT line (image-gen, light, plain relays). Cut with hook-sync-worker-limit-gate for every vendor but codex, whose answer needs the catalogs. The picker's ~0.7 s floor stays: handoff docs/handoffs/2026-10-02-hook-cost-rows.md.

rows.title: edit-conflict-notice over 150 ms a run

Narrowed to its process floor: 195 ms p50 in 24 h at night load 50-60; a probe on a dirty file took 426 ms spread over six git calls, shasum, two jq, one find over the review journal and the library source, none over 65 ms. rows.title: instruction-watch baseline over 150 ms a run
rows.note: Narrowed: a SessionStart hook, once per session. Probe at load 50 with its own state dir: 2.6 s cold (ranked refresh, every snapshot written), 530-600 ms warm, spread over ~20 process starts (find x4, perl, awk, tr, mv, touch), none over 125 ms; the walk itself was cut 2026-10-01. Under 150 ms needs the cached enumeration hook-sync-instruction-watch-check names: the owner's. Not touched: reverts/ holds 84 027 entries, 663 MB (store_size row, another area).

blind_spots.reason: bin/statusline-work-probe.sh writes a row only when a render of the owning chat sees the run start and end within 15 s; 3 of 4 full llm-legs runs overlapping 2026-09-30 02:24-03:03 local left no row

blind_spots.reason: `tests running` and test-history come from statusline work probes, and a `claude -p` session renders no statusline: 03:19 sampled 0 while four night worktrees ran run-suites
blind_spots.would_catch_if: run-suites.sh wrote a start and end line per suite to a journal this doctor reads

blind_spots.what: one instruction-file write journaled by two tripwire records
blind_spots.reason: the guards rule counts each record per file; a record carries no write key (hash@mtime), so a second record of the same write reads as new growth
blind_spots.would_catch_if: each events.jsonl file entry carried its alert key and the guards rule counted a key once

blind_spots.what: the background task type labels Stop hooks filter the payload on
blind_spots.reason: Claude Code 2.1.285 labels an Agent task `subagent` where ask-run-unfinished.sh matched only `local_agent`; the stop journal records the count of live tasks, never their types
blind_spots.would_catch_if: the stop journal recorded each live background task's type, so a hook filter matching none of the labels in use showed

blind_spots.what: An inherited skill-install skip variable overridden by the actual Bash command
blind_spots.reason: The 2026-10-01 guards fixer reproduced HYPERFRAMES_SKIP_SKILLS=1 in the hook environment followed by an explicit =0 init command passing the old gate. Existing growth records identify installed files, not the initializer effective environment; this specific bypass was found by a fixture probe, not established as the historical writer. The dedicated skill-install-scope gate does not emit the instruction gates journal.
blind_spots.would_catch_if: The install-scope gate journaled its effective skip decision and initializer identity, allowing the doctor to correlate allowed init calls with subsequent global SKILL.md growth.

blind_spots.what: A hook floor's share that is machine load rather than hook work
blind_spots.reason: The 2026-10-02 hook-waits fixer read floor:bash:other at 1512 ms in the 1 h window under load average 46-65 (the night's own parallel workers) against 794 ms over 24 h; the same hooks at day load read 605-961 ms. The floor rule judges the last hour with no load context, so a night run measures its own concurrency.
blind_spots.would_catch_if: each floor sample carried the sampler's load average at its call time and the floor drill split its median by load band

blind_spots.what: which hook or worker wrote a repository's loose objects, and whether anything ever packs them
blind_spots.reason: growth samples carry the count and size only; the 2026-10-02 fixer attributed the writer by blob mtimes and content against review-journal .repos mtimes and worker-run workdirs
blind_spots.would_catch_if: the snapshot writers journaled blobs written per repository per call, and the growth sample recorded each repository's last gc (newest pack mtime)

blind_spots.what: why and for how long the instruction watcher was off
blind_spots.reason: watcher/heartbeat is overwritten every tick, so a changed-while-watcher-off record (2026-10-01T12:51:14Z, claude-setup review-floor merge 6413519 at 12:40:33Z) cannot name the off interval or its cause
blind_spots.would_catch_if: the watcher journaled each start and stop (with the reason: Hammerspoon reload, load error, busy tick) beside its heartbeat

blind_spots.what: which registered repository makes commit-journal and review-flow-gate slow
blind_spots.reason: the hook journal times the whole hook only; one tree with 33 704 untracked paths (logo-vectorizer-bench, 0.5-1.5 s a git status) was found 2026-10-03 only by timing each registered tree by hand
